meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: The type a form control's value arrives as
questions.learningObjective: State the type of a form control's value in JavaScript
questions.stem: A marine biologist reads input.value from a number field; what is its type?

options.text: A string, even for numeric inputs

questions.explanation: Form control values are always strings. The belief that numeric inputs yield numbers is false.

questions.topic: How a group of checkboxes is encoded
questions.learningObjective: Encode a group of checkboxes into a request body
questions.stem: Three checkboxes named species are checked; how is the body encoded?
questions.explanation: Form encoding repeats the name for each checked box. Array or comma forms are not default.
questions.hint: Repeat the field name per checked box.

questions.topic: A numeric string in an arithmetic expression
questions.learningObjective: Predict the result of adding a numeric string and a number
questions.stem: In the tank script, '5' + 3 evaluates to what?

options.text: 8, because the string converts to a number
'53', because + concatenates when a string is present

questions.explanation: The + operator concatenates if either operand is a string. Arithmetic conversion does not happen for +.
questions.hint: + concatenates when a string is present.

questions.topic: When the callbacks attached to settled requests run
questions.learningObjective: State when microtasks from settled promises run
questions.stem: When do .then callbacks of an already-settled promise run?

answer.exemplar: They run as microtasks after the current synchronous code finishes and before the next macrotask, never synchronously.

questions.explanation: Promise callbacks are always asynchronous microtasks. They never run inline even if settled.

questions.topic: A response that reports failure
questions.learningObjective: Detect a failed fetch response
questions.stem: A fetch to the tank API returns HTTP 404; does fetch reject?

options.text: No, and response.ok is always true

options.misconception: fetch does not reject on HTTP errors

options.text: No, fetch only rejects on network errors, so check response.ok

questions.explanation: fetch resolves for HTTP errors; response.ok indicates success. Only network failures reject.

questions.topic: Where a malformed body surfaces
questions.learningObjective: Locate where a malformed JSON body surfaces
questions.stem: response.json() is called on a non-JSON body; where does the error surface?

options.text: The json() promise rejects with a SyntaxError
No error; an empty object is returned
options.misconception: invalid JSON does not parse to empty

questions.explanation: Parsing happens in json(), so that promise rejects. fetch has already resolved.

questions.topic: Reading a state variable one rebuild behind
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a state variable reads stale after set
questions.stem: After setCount(count+1), logging count shows the old value; why?

options.text: State updates are asynchronous; the variable reflects the previous render

questions.explanation: State is a snapshot per render; the variable updates on the next render. The setter did not fail.
questions.hint: State is a snapshot per render.

questions.topic: The type a read value has and what + does with it
questions.learningObjective: Convert a read value before arithmetic
questions.stem: A tank temperature is read as '22' and 5 is added; result is '225'. What is the fix?

options.text: Store the value as a number in the DOM
Convert with Number() or unary + before adding

questions.explanation: Converting to a number before + prevents concatenation. DOM values remain strings.

questions.topic: Building the body of a checkbox group
questions.learningObjective: Build a FormData body from a checkbox group
questions.stem: How to build a request body from a group of checked species checkboxes?

answer.exemplar: Iterate the checked boxes and append each value under the shared name to a FormData or URLSearchParams, preserving all selections.

questions.explanation: Appending each checked value under the shared name preserves all selections. A single value loses data.

questions.topic: Joining text and adding after a conversion
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish concatenation from addition after conversion
questions.stem: After converting '5' to 5, what does 5 + 3 produce?

options.misconception: concatenation only if a string is present

options.text: 8, because both operands are now numbers

questions.explanation: Once both operands are numbers, + adds. Concatenation requires a string operand.

questions.topic: Two operators given the same text value
questions.learningObjective: Compare + and - behavior on a text value
questions.stem: Given x='5', what do x+1 and x-1 produce?

options.misconception: + does not convert when a string is present

questions.explanation: + concatenates with a string; - converts to number. The belief that + converts is false.

questions.topic: Synchronous work against queued callbacks
questions.learningObjective: Order synchronous code versus queued callbacks
questions.stem: In the tank script, a sync log and a setTimeout log run; which logs first?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs before any queued callback. Timers cannot preempt the call stack.

questions.topic: Suspending at an await while the script continues
questions.learningObjective: Explain what happens at an await
questions.stem: At an await in an async function, what happens to the rest of the script?

options.text: The whole script blocks until resolution
options.misconception: await does not block the main thread

options.text: The async function suspends and the caller continues synchronously

options.misconception: JS has no threads for this

questions.explanation: await suspends the async function and returns control to the caller. The main thread keeps running.

questions.topic: Reading the body of a failed response
questions.learningObjective: Read an error body from a failed response
questions.stem: How to read the body of a 400 response from fetch?

answer.exemplar: Check response.ok; if false, read response.json() or response.text() to extract the error details before throwing.

questions.explanation: The body is still available on a failed response and must be read explicitly. fetch does not read it for you.

questions.topic: One order arriving twice
questions.learningObjective: Prevent a duplicate order submission
questions.stem: A biologist double-clicks submit and two orders are created; what is the best fix?

options.text: Rely on the server to deduplicate by timestamp

options.misconception: does not stop the second request

options.text: Disable the button after first click and use an idempotency key

questions.explanation: Disabling plus an idempotency key prevents duplicates reliably. Hiding or timestamp dedup is fragile.
questions.hint: Disable button and use idempotency key.

questions.topic: A count that concatenates instead of adding
questions.learningObjective: Fix a count that concatenates strings
questions.stem: A tank count shows '3' + 1 = '31'; how to make it add?

options.text: Convert the count to a number before incrementing

questions.explanation: Converting to a number before incrementing prevents concatenation. Restarting does not change types.

questions.topic: An empty list because the status was never tested
questions.learningObjective: Test an HTTP status before parsing a list
questions.stem: A list renders empty because the 200 check was skipped; what went wrong?

options.text: A non-200 response was parsed as empty data

questions.explanation: Without a status check, error responses may parse as empty. Network or UI are not indicated.

questions.topic: Reading a value and then doing arithmetic with it
questions.learningObjective: Read then convert a value for arithmetic
questions.stem: A value is read from a control and then doubled; what must happen first?

options.text: Convert the string to a number

questions.explanation: Conversion is required before arithmetic. Concatenation or storage does not help.

questions.topic: Counting and then writing a checkbox group's body
questions.learningObjective: Count checked boxes and build the body
questions.stem: A script counts checked boxes but sends only the count, losing which species; what is the fix?

options.text: Send the count as a string
Send each checked value, not just the count

questions.explanation: The body must include each selected value. A count alone loses identity.

questions.topic: Why a control's value is always text
questions.learningObjective: Explain why control values are always text
questions.stem: Why are form control values always text even for number inputs?

answer.exemplar: HTML form controls serialize their values as strings in the DOM and request body, so JavaScript must convert them explicitly for arithmetic.

questions.explanation: The DOM and form encoding are text-based. Conversion is the developer's responsibility.

questions.topic: The type a form control's value arrives as
questions.learningObjective: Use Number() to convert a control value
questions.stem: Which conversion correctly turns input.value into a number?
questions.explanation: Number() converts a numeric string to a number. Addition concatenates; toString is redundant.

questions.topic: How a group of checkboxes is encoded
questions.learningObjective: Parse repeated checkbox values on the server
questions.stem: On the server, how to read repeated species values?

options.text: Collect all values with that name into an array

questions.explanation: All repeated values must be collected. Reading one loses selections.

questions.topic: A numeric string in an arithmetic expression
questions.learningObjective: Use parseInt with a radix
questions.stem: parseInt('08', 10) returns what?
questions.explanation: Radix 10 forces decimal interpretation, yielding 8. Without radix, leading zeros can confuse older parsers.

questions.topic: When the callbacks attached to settled requests run
questions.learningObjective: Use queueMicrotask to defer work
questions.stem: A microtask is queued with queueMicrotask; when does it run?

options.text: After the current task, before the next macrotask

questions.explanation: Microtasks run after the current task and before the next macrotask. They are not inline or deferred to the end.

questions.topic: A response that reports failure
questions.learningObjective: Throw on a non-ok response
questions.stem: How to ensure fetch failures surface as thrown errors?

answer.exemplar: Check response.ok and throw an Error with the status and body when it is false, so callers handle HTTP errors uniformly.

questions.explanation: Throwing on non-ok unifies error handling. fetch alone resolves on HTTP errors.

questions.topic: Where a malformed body surfaces
questions.learningObjective: Catch parse errors separately from network errors
questions.stem: How to distinguish a network failure from a parse failure?

options.text: Network failure rejects fetch; parse failure rejects json()

questions.explanation: Network errors reject fetch; parse errors reject json(). They occur at different stages.
questions.hint: Network rejects fetch; parse rejects json().

questions.topic: Reading a state variable one rebuild behind
questions.learningObjective: Use the functional updater to avoid stale state
questions.stem: How to increment state safely when it depends on previous value?
questions.explanation: The functional updater receives the latest state. Direct increments use stale snapshots.

questions.topic: The type a read value has and what + does with it
questions.learningObjective: Use Number.isNaN to validate conversion
questions.stem: Number('abc') produces NaN; how to detect it?

options.misconception: NaN is not equal to itself
true but not a check for NaN

questions.explanation: Number.isNaN avoids coercion. NaN comparisons are always false.

questions.topic: Building the body of a checkbox group
questions.learningObjective: Serialize a checkbox group as JSON
questions.stem: Sending a checkbox group as JSON requires what?

options.text: An array of selected values in the body

questions.explanation: A JSON array preserves selections. Comma strings or counts lose structure.

questions.topic: Joining text and adding after a conversion
questions.learningObjective: Choose + versus template literal for text
questions.stem: When is template literal better than + for joining text?

answer.exemplar: Template literals are clearer for multi-part strings with embedded expressions, reducing concatenation noise and type coercion mistakes.

questions.explanation: Template literals improve readability and avoid coercion. + is fine for simple cases.

questions.topic: Two operators given the same text value
questions.learningObjective: Predict * behavior on a text value
questions.stem: Given x='5', what does x*2 produce?

options.text: 10, because * converts the string to a number

questions.explanation: * converts operands to numbers. It never concatenates.

questions.topic: Synchronous work against queued callbacks
questions.learningObjective: Avoid blocking the event loop with heavy sync work
questions.stem: Heavy synchronous computation in the tank UI causes what?

options.text: The UI freezes until it completes

questions.explanation: Synchronous work blocks the main thread and freezes the UI. JS does not parallelize.

questions.topic: Suspending at an await while the script continues
questions.learningObjective: Run independent awaits in parallel with Promise.all
questions.stem: Two independent fetches are awaited one after another; how to speed up?

options.text: Await the first, then the second
Use Promise.all to await both together

questions.explanation: Promise.all runs independent fetches concurrently. Serial awaiting wastes time.

questions.topic: Reading the body of a failed response
questions.learningObjective: Clone a response before reading its body
questions.stem: A body is read twice and the second read fails; why?

options.misconception: parsing is fine; stream is consumed

options.text: The server rejects the second read
The first read corrupts the data
The body stream can only be consumed once unless cloned

questions.explanation: Response bodies are streams consumed once. Clone to read multiple times.

questions.topic: One order arriving twice
questions.learningObjective: Generate an idempotency key per submission
questions.stem: How to make a duplicate order submission safe on the server?

answer.exemplar: Accept a client-generated idempotency key with the order and store it uniquely, so a repeated key returns the original result instead of creating a duplicate.

questions.explanation: Idempotency keys deduplicate repeated submissions. Server-side uniqueness is required.

questions.topic: A count that concatenates instead of adding
questions.learningObjective: Use unary plus to convert a count
questions.stem: Which expression converts a string count to a number concisely?
questions.explanation: Unary + converts to number. The other expressions yield string or boolean.

questions.topic: An empty list because the status was never tested
questions.learningObjective: Guard list rendering on response.ok
questions.stem: What should the component do before rendering the list?

options.text: Always set state to the parsed JSON
Check response.ok and handle errors before setting state

questions.explanation: Checking response.ok prevents error bodies from becoming data. Ignoring or retrying forever is wrong.

questions.topic: Reading a value and then doing arithmetic with it
questions.learningObjective: Parse a value with Number() before arithmetic
questions.stem: A control value is added to 10; if it is '5', what result is wrong?
questions.explanation: Without conversion, '5' + 10 yields '510'. Converting gives 15.

questions.topic: Counting and then writing a checkbox group's body
questions.learningObjective: Count and send selected species in one request
questions.stem: A script sends the count but the server needs species names; what is missing?
questions.explanation: The server needs the selected values, not the count. Timestamps and unchecked values do not help.

questions.topic: Why a control's value is always text
questions.learningObjective: Handle a file input's value type
questions.stem: What type is a file input's value, and how to get the file?

answer.exemplar: The value is a string path, but the actual File objects are available via input.files, a FileList, not through value.

questions.explanation: value holds a path string; files holds File objects. Reading value does not give the file.

questions.topic: The type a form control's value arrives as
questions.learningObjective: Read a checkbox's checked state
questions.stem: For a checkbox, which property indicates whether it is selected?

options.misconception: value is the submitted value, not state

questions.explanation: checked is the boolean state. value holds the submitted string.

questions.topic: How a group of checkboxes is encoded
questions.learningObjective: Set default checked boxes in HTML
questions.stem: How to pre-select a checkbox in HTML?
questions.explanation: The checked attribute pre-selects. value and selected do not select checkboxes.

questions.topic: A numeric string in an arithmetic expression
questions.learningObjective: Use Number() instead of parseInt for decimals
questions.stem: parseInt('3.5') returns 3; what returns 3.5?

options.misconception: works but not the focused answer

questions.explanation: Number() preserves decimals. parseInt truncates. parseFloat also works but Number() is the direct choice.

questions.topic: When the callbacks attached to settled requests run
questions.learningObjective: Order promise resolution versus setTimeout
questions.stem: A resolved promise callback and a 0ms setTimeout are queued; which runs first?
questions.explanation: Microtasks drain before the next macrotask, so the promise callback runs first.

questions.topic: A response that reports failure
questions.learningObjective: Read status text from a failed response
questions.stem: How to get the human-readable reason from a failed response?

answer.exemplar: Read response.statusText, which carries the HTTP reason phrase, alongside response.status for the code.

questions.explanation: statusText provides the reason phrase. status alone gives only the code.

questions.topic: Where a malformed body surfaces
questions.learningObjective: Validate JSON before parsing
questions.stem: How to safely handle a possibly malformed JSON body?

options.misconception: length does not imply valid JSON

options.text: Wrap json() in try/catch and handle parse errors

questions.explanation: try/catch around json() handles parse failures. eval is unsafe; length is insufficient.

questions.topic: Reading a state variable one rebuild behind
questions.learningObjective: Avoid reading state immediately after setting
questions.stem: Why does logging state right after setX show the old value?

options.text: The update is scheduled, not applied synchronously

questions.explanation: State updates are scheduled for the next render. The setter is not broken.

questions.topic: The type a read value has and what + does with it
questions.learningObjective: Use parseFloat for decimal control values
questions.stem: parseFloat('3.14') returns what?
questions.explanation: parseFloat returns 3.14. parseInt would truncate to 3.

questions.topic: Building the body of a checkbox group
questions.learningObjective: Build a URLSearchParams from checked boxes
questions.stem: How to build an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body from checked species boxes?

answer.exemplar: Create a URLSearchParams, append each checked value under 'species', and send its toString() as the body with the correct content type.

questions.explanation: URLSearchParams serializes repeated names correctly. Manual string building risks encoding errors.

questions.topic: Joining text and adding after a conversion
questions.learningObjective: Convert then add in one expression
questions.stem: Which expression converts '5' and adds 3 correctly?
questions.explanation: Number('5') + 3 yields 8. The other expressions concatenate, subtract, or multiply.

questions.topic: Two operators given the same text value
questions.learningObjective: Predict == versus === on a text value
questions.stem: Given x='5', what does x == 5 and x === 5 produce?

options.text: true and false, because == coerces but === does not

questions.explanation: == coerces '5' to 5, so true; === checks type, so false. The belief that === coerces is wrong.

questions.topic: Synchronous work against queued callbacks
questions.learningObjective: Use requestIdleCallback to defer heavy work
questions.stem: How to run heavy tank analysis without freezing the UI?

options.text: Run it synchronously in a loop
Defer it with requestIdleCallback or a worker

questions.explanation: Deferring heavy work keeps the UI responsive. Synchronous loops freeze it.

questions.topic: Suspending at an await while the script continues
questions.learningObjective: Explain that await does not block the main thread
questions.stem: Why does await not freeze the browser?

answer.exemplar: await suspends only the async function and returns control to the event loop, so the browser keeps handling user input and rendering.

questions.explanation: await yields to the event loop. It does not block the main thread.
questions.hint: await yields to the event loop.

questions.topic: Reading the body of a failed response
questions.learningObjective: Read an error message from a 4xx response
questions.stem: A 400 response includes a JSON error message; how to show it?

options.text: Parse response.json() and read the error field

questions.explanation: Parsing the body gives the server's error detail. statusText alone may be generic.

questions.topic: One order arriving twice
questions.learningObjective: Disable submit after first click
questions.stem: Simplest client-side guard against double submit?

options.misconception: does not stop a queued click

options.text: Disable the submit button on click

questions.explanation: Disabling the button prevents a second click. Hiding or clearing is less reliable.

questions.topic: A count that concatenates instead of adding
questions.learningObjective: Fix a loop counter that concatenates
questions.stem: A loop uses count = count + 1 where count starts as '0'; result?

options.misconception: + does not convert with a string

questions.explanation: Starting from '0', + concatenates each time. Converting first fixes it.

questions.topic: An empty list because the status was never tested
questions.learningObjective: Add a status check in fetch chain
questions.stem: How to structure a fetch chain to avoid empty lists on errors?

answer.exemplar: Check response.ok and throw before parsing, then parse and set state only in the success path, handling errors in catch.

questions.explanation: Throwing before parsing keeps error bodies out of state. Parsing only on success avoids empty lists.

questions.topic: Reading a value and then doing arithmetic with it
questions.learningObjective: Validate input before arithmetic
questions.stem: Arithmetic on an empty input value yields NaN; what is the right guard?

options.text: Check for empty string before converting

questions.explanation: Checking for empty input before conversion avoids NaN. Defaulting hides missing data.

questions.topic: Counting and then writing a checkbox group's body
questions.learningObjective: Validate that at least one box is checked
questions.stem: Before submitting a checkbox group, what should be verified?

options.text: At least one box is checked

questions.explanation: Requiring at least one selection matches typical intent. All or none are extremes.

questions.topic: Why a control's value is always text
questions.learningObjective: Convert a value before comparing to a number
questions.stem: Comparing input.value === 5 is always false; why?

options.text: Because 5 is not a valid input
Because value is a string and === checks type

questions.explanation: value is a string, so strict equality with a number is false. === does not coerce.
